verdict_text:
NO

The merge computes `tmp = base + λ(ft1 - base)` and then `tmp + λ(ft2 - tmp)`, i.e. it applies the second task vector against the already-updated `tmp` (equivalently `(1-λ)·tmp + λ·ft2`) rather than against the unmodified base. This violates the ordering requirement in step 2 and the "Why it is meaningful" clause, which specify `out[X] = base[X] + λ(ft1[X]-base[X]) + λ(ft2[X]-base[X])` — both task vectors must be taken relative to the original base, not composed sequentially. Algebraically, `tmp + λ(ft2-tmp) = (1-λ)base + λft1 + λft2 - λ²(ft1-base)`, which differs from the required `base + λ(ft1-base) + λ(ft2-base)` by a term of order λ², so this is not just a reordering of additions (which the grading tolerates) but a different formula.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
